en: Three: The Besieged City
zh: 第三章　围城

en: From late 2000 to 2002, I lived in a socialist-era, five-story brick building in Xicheng District. I rented my one-bedroom apartment from a woman named Art Soldier, who worked in the state film bureau. She and her husband had moved into a new commodity apartment in a nearby high-rise development. Meanwhile many of her former neighbors, who remained in the older work-unit housing, launched a variety of

projects. Zhuangxiu means to fix up or redecorate and became a craze that besieged the city. The sounds of the neighborhood permeated my reprieve from Beijing’s streets: vendors’ calls from the vegetable market outside the enclosed balcony where I hung laundry to dry; wind banging screens and hissing its way around window frames; the grunts of sex on the other side of my bedroom wall; the lonely tune of someone whistling in the dim, concrete stairwell. But more than any other sound, I awoke to that of drilling, hammering, and sawing. Entrepreneurs on the nearby thoroughfare renovated their shops and restaurants. Some boasted bright lights, shiny glass and metal, and synthetic color schemes. Others cultivated a more pastoral aesthetic, such as the restaurants whose managers hired folk artists to paint landscape murals on their exteriors. The character
(demolish) showed up in broad swaths, its white paint dripping down walls, like a command for the city to translate its old appearance into something new.
zh: 从2000年底到2002年，我住在西城区一栋社会主义时期的五层砖楼里。我从一个名叫文艺兵的女人那里租下一套一居室公寓，她在国家电影局工作。她和丈夫已经搬进附近一栋高层楼盘的新商品房。与此同时，她的许多仍住在老旧单位宿舍的前邻居纷纷启动各种装修工程。装修的意思是修理或重新装饰，它成为一种围困城市的狂热。社区的声音渗入我从北京街头回到的喘息空间：封闭阳台外菜市场的叫卖声——我在那里晾衣服；风拍打纱窗、绕着窗框呼啸的声音；卧室墙另一侧的性爱呻吟；昏暗混凝土楼梯间里某人孤独的口哨曲调。但最常把我唤醒的，是钻孔、锤击和锯木的声响。附近大道上的店主翻新店铺和餐馆。有些以明亮的灯光、闪亮的玻璃和金属以及合成色彩为傲。另一些则培养更田园的审美，例如有些餐馆经理雇民间艺人在外墙绘制山水壁画。“拆”（chai）字大片出现，白漆顺着墙壁滴下，仿佛是命令这座城市把旧貌改写成新颜。

en: Aspirational dramas unfolded on the television screen in my darkened apartment, where I retreated after long days of commuting around the city for classes, interviews, and meetings. Amid Hong Kong soap operas of the rich and famous, South Korean family sagas, and Mainland dynastic costume dramas, I caught episodes of

when the ten-part series reran on China Central tv. Based on a 1947 novel by Qian Zhongshu, the adaptation first aired in 1991, gaining wide viewership and popularity. The title of the novel, translated as
or

, entered 1990s Chinese lexicon along with words like “stock market,” “privacy,” and “mba.” It became a popular metaphor referring to marriage, feeling stuck, striving under false pretenses, and human dissatisfaction.

Qian’s satirical novel, whose depiction of bourgeois life fell out of print under Mao, tells the story of urban middle-class Fang Hongjian. After frittering years away in Europe under the pretext of advanced study, he runs out of money, buys a fake doctoral diploma from the United States (the name of the granting institution transliterated into Chinese is Charlatan University), and returns to Shanghai in 1937 on the eve of World War II. Fang enters into one after another of failed relationships with women, who range from a fiancée in an arranged marriage to a female classmate who earned a Ph.D. in Europe before getting caught as a plagiarist. His continual longing for what he does not currently possess turns into an everyday tragicomedy of human isolation likened to the Chinese condition of Shanghai in the late 1930s, an extraterritorial city of surreptitious freedoms but one governed by foreign concessions and beset by the Japanese.
zh: 在我昏暗的公寓里，电视屏幕上上演着充满向往与追求的电视剧——那是我为上课、采访和会议在城市里奔波一整天后退守的地方。在香港富豪名流肥皂剧、韩国家庭史诗剧和内地古装剧之间，我赶上《围城》十集电视剧在中央电视台重播。该剧改编自钱锺书1947年的小说，1991年首播，获得广泛收视和欢迎。小说标题被译作 The Besieged City 或 Fortress Besieged，与“股市”“隐私”以及“MBA”等词一起进入1990年代的中国词汇。它成为一个流行隐喻，指涉婚姻、受困感、在虚假前提下奋斗以及人的不满足。

钱锺书的讽刺小说在毛泽东时代因描写资产阶级生活而绝版，讲述城市中产阶级方鸿渐的故事。他以进修访学为名在欧洲虚度数年，花光钱后从美国买了一张假博士文凭（授予学位的机构中文译名为“克莱登大学”），于第二次世界大战前夕的1937年回到上海。方鸿渐接连卷入与女性的失败关系，从包办婚姻的未婚妻，到在欧洲获得博士学位、后来被抓出抄袭的女同学。他对当下所无之物的持续渴望，变成一部关于人际孤立的日常悲喜剧，被比作1930年代末上海的“中国处境”——一座享有隐秘自由的治外法权城市，却由外国租界统治，并受日本侵扰。

en: The opening sequence of each television episode shows the original edition of Qian’s book, followed by translations published in the United States, Soviet Union, France, Germany, Japan, and Taiwan. A voiceover intones, “People surrounded inside the city want to flee out, people outside of the city want to rush in; in the face of marriage or occupation, such is human desire.” This series tagline alludes to the French proverb Qian used as epigraph to his novel: “Marriage is like a fortress besieged: those who are outside want to get in, and those who are inside want to get out.”
Lost in this itinerary of translation is the uncanny way that Qian’s title in Chinese provides a metaphor that resonates into both past and future. A literal translation of

is “surrounded cities,” evoking images of the old walled imperial capital, the colonial city besieged by Western powers during the Opium Wars, the wartime city under Japanese control, the revolutionary city surrounded as in Mao’s injunction by the purifying countryside, and the new millennial city rife with construction attempting to overcome this siege of history by “linking tracks with the world.”
zh: 每一集电视剧的片头都展示钱锺书小说的原版，以及在美国、苏联、法国、德国、日本和台湾出版的译本。旁白吟诵：“城里的人想逃出去，城外的人想冲进来；面对婚姻或职业，人的欲望便是如此。”这句系列宣传语暗指钱锺书用作小说题记的法语谚语：“婚姻像一座被围困的城堡：城外的人想冲进去，城里的人想逃出来。”
在这一翻译旅程中失落的，是钱锺书的中文标题所提供的那种诡异隐喻力量——它同时回响于过去与未来。“围城”的字面翻译是“被包围的城市”，令人想起旧日有城墙的帝国首都、鸦片战争中被西方列强围困的殖民城市、战时受日本控制的城市、被毛泽东所谓具有净化作用的乡村所包围的革命城市，以及新千年里到处是建设、试图通过“与世界接轨”来克服这一历史围困的城市。

en: Marriage enters the metaphorical conceit in relation to questions of fidelity and modernity. What should one believe in and remain loyal to: tradition, family, romance, revolution, socialism, capitalism, nation, or world? In the words of the docent in my neighborhood museum whose logic jumped from censorship to divorce to discrimination to immigration: you’d be a fool to believe someone would love you for your whole life.
captures a sense of caution about the promise of any ideological arrangement.
zh: 婚姻进入这一隐喻构思，与忠诚和现代性的问题相关。人应当相信并忠于什么：传统、家庭、爱情、革命、社会主义、资本主义、民族，还是世界？用我家附近博物馆那位讲解员的话说——他的逻辑从审查跳到离婚，再到歧视，再到移民：你要是相信有人会爱你一辈子，那就是傻瓜。《围城》捕捉到对所有意识形态安排之承诺的警觉。

en: As I was pulled into serving as a Chinese-English interpreter in several transnational encounters between Chinese artists and curators from abroad, the phrase

wound its way into our discussions. Artists invoked it to describe their relationship with the international art market. Precariously balanced against their desire to “get out” was that of returning and gaining respect at home. As translators of Chinese and Western aesthetics, they might serve as exemplars of cosmopolitanism or become susceptible to accusations of excessive fidelity to one or another artistic tradition.
zh: 当我在中国艺术家与海外策展人的若干跨国相遇中被拉去担任中英口译时，“围城”一词蜿蜒进入我们的讨论。艺术家用它描述自己与国际艺术市场的关系。与“走出去”的渴望如履薄冰地相平衡的，是回来并在国内获得尊重的渴望。作为中国与西方美学的翻译者，他们可能成为世界主义的典范，也可能轻易被指责对某一艺术传统过度忠诚。

en: Serving as an interpreter put a new spin on the perennial if falsely dichotomous insider-outsider dilemma of ethnographers.

Did I share greater insider status with curators from the United States or with Chinese artists I’d spent nominally more time with? What were the ethics of translation that became part of curatorial selection?

Who might I betray in the exchange, given the disciplinary tension between art and anthropology, in which an anthropologist might be called on to interpret linguistic and cultural nuance but not artistic value? The more I became involved in these zones of cultural encounter, the more aware I grew of the transnational,
rules of the game and resulting exclusion of particular kinds of artists.
zh: 担任口译员，为民族志学者由来已久却虚假二分的内外困境增添了新的转折。
我与美国策展人，还是与名义上相处更久的中国艺术家，共享更多“内部人”身份？构成策展选择的翻译伦理是什么？
鉴于艺术与人类学之间的学科张力——人类学家可能被要求解释语言和文化细微之处，却不被要求判断艺术价值——我可能在交换中背叛谁？我越深入这些文化相遇地带，就越意识到跨国性的男女游戏规则，以及由此对特定类型艺术家的排斥。

en: Participants in these encounters struggled with the constraints of a world organized according to a nation-state system. This framework structured the institutions they represented, as well as the ones they aspired to be accepted by, or the ones they had trained in. These institutions included museums, cultural organizations, international exhibitions, and art academies, as well as embassies that supported cultural exchange projects and issued or denied visas for artists to travel. The curators and artists I interpreted for readily apprehended and passionately debated the legacy of colonialism and racism within these institutions. They articulated visions of minority cosmopolitanism, even as they silently reiterated other powerful social distinctions in making art worthy of the world stage. Taking on the task of the translator presented a unique opportunity for ethnographic participant-observation but also implicated me in the behind-the-scenes of cultural production. Within the circles of male artists who dominated the Chinese contemporary art scene, I learned about the girlfriends, Chinese and foreign, who had served as translators and cultural brokers. One artist had gone through so many that others jokingly referred to him as Lianhe Guo, or United Nations. At one point, in my weariness with the sexual innuendo that was part of the scene, I fantasized about creating a performance piece in a photography studio where I would invite male artists to take wedding photographs with me. These mental theatrics provided an outlet for my own aggravation but more importantly revealed multidirectional anxieties produced by striving to be of the world: a wariness of being used, of being someone’s ticket in or out, of being judged inauthentic.
zh: 这些相遇的参与者挣扎于一个按民族国家体系组织的世界所施加的限制。这一框架结构了他们所代表的机构，也结构了他们渴望被其接纳的机构，或他们接受训练的机构。这些机构包括博物馆、文化组织、国际展览和艺术学院，也包括支持文化交流项目、为艺术家签发或拒发旅行签证的大使馆。我为其口译的策展人和艺术家轻易理解并激烈辩论这些机构内部的殖民主义与种族主义遗产。他们阐述少数者世界主义的愿景，却在让艺术配得上世界舞台的过程中，默默重申其他强大的社会区分。承担译者的任务，为民族志参与观察提供了独特机会，但也把我卷入文化生产的幕后。在主导中国当代艺术界的男性艺术家圈子里，我了解到那些充当翻译和文化中介的中外女友。一位艺术家的女友换得太频繁，其他人开玩笑称他为“联合国”。有时，我对场景中性暗示的厌倦达到顶点，便幻想创作一件行为作品：在一间摄影棚里，我会邀请男性艺术家与我拍摄婚纱照。这些脑内戏剧是我气愤情绪的出口，但更重要的是，它们揭示了努力“属于世界”所产生的多向焦虑：害怕被利用，害怕成为某人进入或离开的入场券，害怕被判断为不真实。

en: Authorship and Originality
zh: 作者身份与原创性

en: In the besieged city of zhuangxiu, efforts to make Beijing global and of foreign curators to find Chinese artists who would globalize their institutions, the artwork of Wang Yin highlights tensions in the debate about what counts as art. It translated styles like the folk murals outside restaurants near my apartment into global contemporary art. His experiments with authorship and originality also reflected post-Mao rearrangements of social relations and subjectivities around notions of labor, property, and community. In 2000, Wang Yin began working with a village artist from Henan Province. He hired the painter, who specialized in colorful motifs common in rural decorative murals, to work in his Tongzhou studio. The painter executed scenes from his craftsman’s repertoire on stretched canvas or black flannel. In

. 7, his landscape combines mist-shrouded mountains, green valleys, lotus flowers, and modern high-rise buildings in the verdant distance. On top of this landscape, Wang Yin painted in broad, expressionist brushstrokes a large, grey-toned figure. His muscular mass reclines barefoot against the pine tree in the foreground, head jutting forward at an awkward angle. His body remains incompletely realized, with parts of the background, a spot of red and blotch of green, showing through a forearm and thigh. The painting presents an encounter of idioms from differently organized art worlds—decorative mural and modernist oil painting—each of which take away part of the other, in a pastiche recognized by the contemporary art market as the conceptual work of Wang Yin, not the anonymous painter who “prepared” his canvases.
zh: 在装修围城、北京走向全球的努力，以及外国策展人寻找能使其机构全球化的中国艺术家之际，王音的作品凸显了关于什么才算艺术的辩论中的紧张。他的作品把我公寓附近餐馆外墙的民间壁画之类风格转译成全球当代艺术。他对作者身份与原创性的实验，也反映了毛泽东之后围绕劳动、财产和社区观念对社会关系与主体性的重新安排。2000年，王音开始与一位来自河南的乡村画师合作。他雇这位擅长乡村装饰壁画中常见彩色图案的画师，在他的通州工作室工作。画师在绷好的画布或黑色法兰绒上绘制其工匠技艺中熟悉的场景。《2000年，第7号》中的山水融合了云雾缭绕的群山、翠绿山谷、荷花和远处苍翠中的现代高楼。在这幅山水之上，王音以宽大、表现主义的笔触画了一个巨大的灰色调人物。他肌肉发达的身躯赤脚斜倚在前景的松树上，头以别扭的角度向前探出。他的身体仍未完全成形，背景的一部分——一块红色和一块绿色——从一条前臂和大腿处透出。这幅画呈现了来自不同组织方式的艺术世界的语汇相遇——装饰壁画与现代主义油画——彼此都消减了对方的一部分，形成一种被当代艺术市场认定为王音观念作品的拼贴，而非那位为其“准备”画布的匿名画师的拼贴。

en: The base layer of

(plate 8) presents a brightly pigmented tableau of traditional Chinese imagery: rushing waterfalls, a junk sailing down a river, a pagoda in the distance, soaring cranes symbolizing longevity. Wang has then obliterated the scene with blunt, thickly applied repetitive strokes in muted shades of brown that cover the entire canvas. The painting’s title alludes to the massive sandstorm that enveloped Beijing in March 2002, the result of increasing desertification in China’s northwest, obliquely referencing fraught relations between city and country and the politics of reduced visibility. A reverse layering seems to occur in

(figure 3.01), as peonies blossom over an abstract color field, although small details of drips and washes over the flowers suggest multiple, successive overpaintings. For this piece, Wang asked his village counterpart to execute a design of flowers receding to the horizon, creating a sense of deep perspectival space. The peony flickers between folk symbol of wealth and minimalist motif in dialogue with modernist ideas of abstraction, replication, and alienation. The hierarchical separation of manual and mental, rural and urban labor becomes manifest in a painting largely in the hand of one painter but under the direction and bearing the name of another.
zh: 《沙尘暴》（图版8）的底层是一幅色彩明亮的中国传统意象图景：奔腾的瀑布、顺流而下的帆船、远处的宝塔、象征长寿的飞鹤。王音随后用钝拙、厚涂、重复的笔触，以柔和的棕色覆盖整幅画布，抹去这一场景。画名暗指2002年3月笼罩北京的大规模沙尘暴——中国西北日益严重的沙漠化的结果，迂回地指涉城乡之间紧张的关系和能见度降低的政治。《花》（图3.01）中似乎发生了反向分层：牡丹在抽象色域上绽放，尽管花朵上的滴痕和晕染等小细节暗示多次连续的覆盖绘制。为这件作品，王音请他的乡村合作者绘制一幅向地平线退去的花卉图案，营造出纵深透视空间感。牡丹在民间财富象征与极简主义母题之间闪烁，与现代主义的抽象、复制和异化观念对话。脑力劳动与体力劳动、城市劳动与乡村劳动的等级分离，在一幅主要由一位画师动手、却由另一位指导并署名的画作中显露出来。

en: I first met Wang Yin while interpreting for a group of curators from the United States as they toured Beijing artists’ studios. As Wang discussed his work, he spoke consciously about disrupting the myth of the autonomous artist, undermining notions of originality, and even making obvious the social economy of art by hiring a painter to work for him. The reassertion of the autonomous artist over the anonymous folk painter in

meeting with the curators remained a silent subtext. Wang’s hand or conceptual input altered the paintings in a way that transformed them into globally recognized art, while the portability of works on canvas rather than walls enabled them to enter this system of exchange. In his 1942 “Talks at the Yan’an Conference on Literature and Art,” Mao Zedong exhorted the nation’s “cultural army” to stand with the people, to get to know them in order to represent China in its revolutionary struggle: “We must use what belongs to workers, peasants, and soldiers themselves, and therefore, the task of learning from workers, peasants, and soldiers comes before the task of educating them.”

Wang reversed Mao’s call that artists go to the countryside to learn from the people, hiring the people instead to come to his studio. This mode of cultural production drew on and painted over a socialist understanding of art as communal effort.
zh: 我第一次遇见王音，是在为一群美国策展人参观北京艺术家工作室时担任口译。王音谈论自己的作品时，有意识地讲到打破自主艺术家的神话、削弱原创性观念，甚至通过雇用一个画师为其工作，让艺术的社会经济机制变得显而易见。然而在与策展人会面时，自主艺术家相对于匿名民间画师的优越地位被再次确立，仍是无声的潜台词。王音的手或观念投入改变了画作，使其转化为全球认可的艺术；而画布作品相对于墙面作品的可携带性，使它们得以进入这一交换体系。1942年，毛泽东在《在延安文艺座谈会上的讲话》中号召全国的“文化军队”与人民站在一起，了解人民，以便在革命斗争中表现中国：“我们必须用属于工人、农民和士兵自己的东西，因此，向工人、农民、士兵学习的任务先于教育他们的任务。”
王音颠倒了毛泽东要艺术家下乡向人民学习的号召，改而雇用人民来到他的工作室。这种文化生产方式挪用并覆盖了把艺术理解为集体努力的社会主义观念。

en: In her study of the translated modernity of early twentieth-century Chinese literature, Lydia Liu writes, “Strictly speaking, comparative scholarship that aims to cross cultures can do nothing but translate.... But leaving aside the marital trope of fidelity and the logocentric notion of truth—concepts that readily lend themselves to deconstructionist criticism—what else do we know or can we say about translation and its implications for cross-cultural understanding?”

This chapter considers her question in relation to Chinese contemporary art as a dialogic construction. The work of Wang Yin and the hired folk painter provides a visual metaphor for the formal, linguistic, and cultural mediations that occur in artistic production and valuation. It demonstrates the making of art as a process that involves multiple social actors but also the superimpositions, alterations, and erasures that result from their exchange.
zh: 刘禾在关于二十世纪初中国文学翻译现代性的研究中写道：“严格说来，旨在跨越文化的比较研究除了翻译之外别无他法……但是，暂且抛开忠实的婚姻隐喻和逻各斯中心的真理观念——这些概念很容易成为解构主义批评的对象——关于翻译及其对跨文化理解的含义，我们还能知道什么、还能说什么呢？”
本章把她的问题放在中国当代艺术作为一种对话性建构的语境中考察。王音与受雇民间画师的作品，为艺术生产和评价中发生的形式、语言与文化中介提供了一个视觉隐喻。它表明艺术制作是一个涉及多重社会行动者的过程，也涉及他们在交换中造成的叠印、修改和擦除。

en: In the encounters I interpreted for, the curators looked at the work shown to them and dialogically, through statement and question, tried to frame the images in terms of their developing exhibit ideas. The artists, in turn, provided personal, historical, and cultural context for their work. In this interplay of linguistic and pictorial, a precursor to the relationship of art and wall text in a museum exhibit, the curators and artists looked and talked and mutually interpreted the art at hand. They also depended on my Chinese-English interpretation, and my subjectivity entered the discussion, innocuously in moments of “good” translation and disruptively in moments of “bad” translation. In the most egregious case of the latter, I expressed (in English only) frustration with an artist’s use of sexualized female figures. My fatigue with the abundance of this type of imagery, exacerbated by recognition of very few female artists, wore through. The curators responded to my remark by pushing the artist to explain his use of this imagery. He gave short, elusive replies about sexual repression under Communism and desire unleashed in its aftermath. Later, one of the curators chastised me, saying that my tone of voice had caused the artist to shut down. When I later ran into the artist at exhibit openings, his antagonist stance made it clear that he too blamed me for interfering.
zh: 在我担任口译的相遇中，策展人观看展示给他们的作品，并通过陈述和提问进行对话，试图根据自己正在形成的展览思路框定图像。艺术家则反过来提供作品的个人、历史和文化背景。在这种语言与图像的相互作用中——它是博物馆展览中艺术与墙面文字关系的前身——策展人和艺术家观看、交谈，并相互阐释眼前的艺术。他们还依赖我的中英口译，而我的主体性进入了讨论：在“好”翻译的时刻无害，在“坏”翻译的时刻具有破坏性。后者的一个最恶劣案例，是我（只用英语）表达了对一位艺术家使用性化女性形象的不满。我对这类图像泛滥的厌倦，加之意识到得到认可的女性艺术家寥寥无几，终于按捺不住。策展人回应我的评论，逼艺术家解释他对这类图像的使用。他给出简短而含糊的回答，说这是共产主义下的性压抑及其后释放的欲望。后来，一位策展人斥责我，说我的语气让艺术家闭了嘴。后来我在展览开幕式上遇到这位艺术家时，他敌对的态度清楚表明，他也怪罪我干涉。

en: Art in a Global Age
zh: 全球时代的艺术

en: I was first drawn into the role of interpreter in April 2001, after asking an independent Chinese curator if I could follow along on the studio tours he often arranged for curators visiting from abroad. Frequently called on as a consultant on Chinese avant-garde art, Huang Du had recently served on advisory committees for biennials in the United States, Cuba, Argentina, and Italy.
For him, this work represented an important sideline to his decade-long employment as an editor at
(Fine arts), the official journal of the Chinese Association of Artists. In a juggling act of professional identities, Huang promoted to his international colleagues the kind of art that

had denounced in a series of articles that year criticizing nudity in performance art and other “immoral” forms of art. He enthusiastically spoke the language of European cultural theory, often dropping words in English like
, and

into conversations in Chinese. Huang Du invited me to join him and Philippe Vergne, curator of visual arts for the Walker Art Center in Minneapolis, through long days of Beijing studio visits. Vergne, originally from France, was on his first visit to China. He had four days to do initial research for a 2003 exhibit to feature artwork from Brazil, China, India, Japan, South Africa, and Turkey, part of a global initiative launched by the Walker in 1998. Huang managed conversation in English quite well, but as the first day progressed, he encouraged me to take on the task of interpreting between Vergne and the artists. Huang continued to weigh in on both sides, in English and Chinese.
zh: 我第一次被拉入口译角色是在2001年4月，当时我请求一位中国独立策展人，让我跟随他经常为海外来访策展人安排的工作室参观。黄笃经常被聘为中国先锋艺术顾问，最近刚担任美国、古巴、阿根廷和意大利双年展的顾问委员会成员。

对他而言，这份工作是他在《美术》——中国美术家协会官方刊物——任职编辑十年间的一项重要副业。黄笃在职业身份之间耍杂技，向国际同行推介的正是《美术》那年在一系列文章中谴责的艺术：那些文章批评行为艺术中的裸体和其他“不道德”艺术形式。他热情地说着欧洲文化理论的语言，常在中文交谈中夹带 postmodern、simulacra、implosion、intersubjectivity 等英文词。黄笃邀请我和明尼阿波利斯沃克艺术中心视觉艺术策展人菲利普·韦尔涅一起，度过漫长数日的北京工作室参观。韦尔涅原籍法国，首次访问中国。他有四天时间为2003年一个将展出巴西、中国、印度、日本、南非和土耳其艺术的展览做初步研究——这是沃克中心1998年发起的全球计划的一部分。黄笃的英语交流能力相当不错，但第一天进行下去，他鼓励我承担韦尔涅与艺术家之间的口译工作。黄笃继续用中英文在两边发表意见。

en: Philippe Vergne introduced the future Walker show to the artists he met as one that would feature “non-Western” artists. In later catalogue texts, he and contributing colleagues refer to their organizing principle in terms of globality or globalization, citing theoretical influences ranging from Arjun Appadarai to Saskia Sassen, Homi Bhabha to Stuart Hall. Vergne balanced ideas developed by these scholars of modernity, urbanism, postcolonialism, and cultural studies with the concerns of the institution he represented in China and elsewhere in his research travels. The Walker Art Center, one of many foreign art institutions to send curators to China to learn more about its contemporary art scene, had a particular rationale for the exhibit that became

children: How Latitudes Become Forms: Art in a Global Age

en: (February–May 2003).
zh: 菲利普·韦尔涅向他遇到的艺术家介绍未来的沃克展览时，说它将展出“非西方”艺术家。在后来的图录文章中，他和参与撰稿的同事以全球性或全球化表述其组织原则，引用从阿尔君·阿帕杜莱、萨斯基娅·萨森到霍米·巴巴、斯图亚特·霍尔的理论影响。韦尔涅把这些现代性、城市主义、后殖民主义和文化研究学者的观念，与他所代表机构的关切相平衡——在中国以及其他研究旅行地也是如此。沃克艺术中心是众多派策展人来中国了解当代艺术现场的外国艺术机构之一，它对最终成为《纬度如何成为形式：全球时代的艺术》（2003年2月—5月）的展览有一套特定理由。

en: Museum staff and consultants, involved in their own discussion of what it meant to be a global city, wanted to better represent the diversity of Minneapolis. Kathy Halbreich, director of the Walker Art Center, writes: “Minneapolis is one of the nation’s most rapidly changing cities and is now more culturally, ethnically, and economically diverse than ever before.... To be a more locally engaged institution, we need to become more sensitive to the increasingly inter-connected world reflected in the demographics of our own community.”
zh: 博物馆员工与顾问们参与各自关于何为全球城市的讨论，希望更好地呈现明尼阿波利斯的多样性。沃克艺术中心馆长凯西·哈尔布雷希写道：“明尼阿波利斯是全国变化最快的城市之一，如今在文化、族裔和经济上比以往任何时候都更加多元……要成为一个更深入本地参与的机构，我们需要对自身社区人口结构所反映的日益互联的世界更加敏感。”

en: Huang Du and the artists with whom we met could converse fluently about international contemporary art trends. Philippe Vergne spoke easily about their work in relation to particular schools, movements, and forms, but he also strove to understand historical, cultural details less familiar to him but relevant to the artwork he encountered. Early in his visit, he asked an artist about his use of the color red by noting possible associations of it with objects like Mao’s Little Red Book. The artist purposefully ignored the political implications of the question by giving a strictly formal answer. I also found myself rephrasing in English expressions of frustration by artists like Zhu Jia, who remained suspicious of being chosen for international exhibitions simply for their nationality. I tried to provide context, ranging from decades-old debates about urban planning in Beijing to the political history of cabbage distribution, in relation to the works of art we viewed. Over dinner one evening, I translated the shared desire of Huang and Vergne for global art as a stage for artistic exchange where it was no longer necessary to flag artists by their national identities.
zh: 黄笃和我们见到的艺术家都能流畅谈论国际当代艺术趋势。菲利普·韦尔涅也能轻松地把他们的作品与特定流派、运动和形式联系起来，但他同时努力理解那些他不太熟悉、却与所遇作品相关的历史与文化细节。访问之初，他问一位艺术家为什么使用红色，提到红色可能与毛泽东的《红宝书》等物有关。那位艺术家有意无视问题的政治含义，给出纯形式的回答。我也发现自己要用英语重述朱加等艺术家的不满——他们始终怀疑自己入选国际展览仅仅因为国籍。我试图提供背景，从数十年前关于北京城市规划的辩论，到白菜分配的政治史，与我们所看的作品联系起来。某天晚餐时，我翻译了黄笃和韦尔涅的共同愿望：让全球艺术成为艺术交流的舞台，在那里不再有必要以国族身份标示艺术家。

en: At this point, I broke into the conversation to argue for the importance of cultural specificity in the midst of this hopeful vision. I reminded them of the years of training in Chinese language, history, and culture that had come into play as I interpreted the ground that helped them place various artworks into curatorial discourses of globalization, appropriation, or modernity, to draw attention to the complex processes underlying this translation effort of fitting “original” intentions together with their complements. In the equation of Chinese X = English Y, the trick of the equal sign (the more forgettable, the job better done) makes the passage to formal synonymy seem smooth and transparent when it also contains histories of inequality. What, for example, the director of the Walker Art Center and the director of the World Art Museum at Beijing’s Millennium Monument might mean by reference to “global art/

” emerges from specific, nonequivalent understandings about the role of art in the global system and its modern nation-state components. While there may be an “international language of art” that crosses national borders, those who speak it do so from different subject positions and fields of reference, some of which have more canonical power in the world than others.
zh: 此时，我插话为文化特殊性在这幅充满希望的愿景中的重要性辩护。我提醒他们，正是凭借多年在汉语、中国历史与文化方面的训练，我才能阐释相关背景，帮助他们把各种作品置入全球化、挪用或现代性的策展话语；我想让他们注意，这一把“原初”意图与其对应物拼合起来的翻译努力，底层过程何其复杂。在汉语 X = 英语 Y 的等式中，等号的把戏（越不引人注意，工作做得越好）使通向形式同义的道路显得平滑透明，而它同时包含不平等的诸历史。例如，沃克艺术中心馆长与北京中华世纪坛世界艺术馆馆长各自提到“全球艺术／世界艺术”（shijie yishu）时，其含义源自对艺术在全球体系及现代民族国家组成部分中之角色的特定而不对等的理解。尽管可能存在一种跨越国界的“国际艺术语言”，那些言说它的人却从不同的主体位置和参照场域出发，其中一些在世界上的权威性高于另一些。

en: The Language of Art/Yishu
zh: “art／艺术”的语言

en: In her analysis of literature, national culture, and translated modernity in semicolonial China, Lydia Liu challenges conventional understandings of translation with her concept of translingual practice. This practice, which she traces through neologisms introduced into Chinese from Japanese and European languages, accounts for the meaningful alterations that occur when words travel through time and cultural-linguistic space. As Liu explains, she “examines the process by which new words, new meanings, discourses, and modes of representation arise, circulate, and acquire legitimacy within the host language due to, or in spite of, the latter’s contact/collision with the guest language.”
For example, the contemporary Chinese term for “art” (
) is as a return graphic loan. The two pictographs for
and

once formed a classical Chinese-character compound that signified the broad range of skills—in social rites, music, archery, chariotry, literature, and mathematics—Confucian scholars were expected to master. The character compound was then borrowed by the Japanese to translate the modern European meaning of “art” and then reintroduced through Japan into modern Chinese.

I translated “art” as yishu as if they were interchangeable, yet a long history of travel, profound anxiety about the future of Asia in the world, and Western and Japanese colonial incursions preceded my ability to do so. Related twentieth-century ideological building blocks include
/culture (return graphic loan),
/modern (Sino-Japanese-European loanword), and
/museum (neologism derived from missionary-Chinese texts).
zh: 刘禾在分析半殖民地中国的文学、民族文化与翻译现代性时，以“跨语际实践”概念挑战对翻译的常规理解。这一实践——她通过从日语和欧洲语言引入汉语的新词加以追踪——解释了词语穿越时间和文化语言空间时发生的有意义变化。如刘禾所解释，她“考察新词、新意义、话语和再现方式如何由于宿主语言与宾客语言的接触／碰撞，或尽管存在这种接触／碰撞，仍在宿主语言中产生、流通并获得合法性”。
例如，当代汉语中的“艺术”一词是一个回流的书写借词。“艺”和“术”两个字曾构成一个古汉语复合词，指儒家学者应掌握的广泛技能——礼、乐、射、御、书、数。该复合词随后被日语借用，用以翻译欧洲现代意义上的“art”，再经由日本重新引入现代汉语。
我把“art”译为“艺术”，仿佛二者可以互换，然而在这一能力形成之前，已经存在漫长的旅行史、对亚洲在世界中未来的深切焦虑，以及西方和日本的殖民入侵。相关的二十世纪意识形态基石还包括文化／culture（回流的书写借词）、现代／modern（汉日欧借词）和博物馆／museum（源自传教士中文文本的新造词）。

en: In the period of Liu’s analysis of Chinese literature, 1900–37, Chinese writers participated in a multitude of translingual practices because of the conditions of imperialism. In order to resist, they turned to words and ideas borrowed from the West, often via Japan as the major interpreter of Western modernity for China. They relentlessly translated European texts into Chinese, carving a largely one-way channel. Liu asks of this passionate, sometimes desperate engagement, “Is there a difference between colonization and self-colonization? If so, what does the difference tell us about the meaning of agency?”

She also argues that while Chinese more often serves as host language to a Western guest (curators in the case at hand) than the other way around, it is nonetheless a host that does not simply receive, but changes the guest language through approximate translation and insertion into Chinese texts and contexts. A long history of cultural encounter has shaped this biculturality, linguistic copresence of East and West, or coauthorship performed through everyday language use.
zh: 在刘禾所分析的中国文学时期，即1900至1937年，中国作家因帝国主义处境而参与了大量跨语际实践。为了抵抗，他们转向从西方借来的词语和观念，且往往经由作为西方现代性主要阐释者的日本。他们不懈地把欧洲文本译成中文，开辟出一条基本单向的渠道。刘禾对这一热切、有时绝望的投入问道：“殖民与自我殖民之间是否存在差异？如果存在，这一差异告诉我们能动性的意义是什么？”
她还论证，虽然中文更经常充当西方宾客的宿主语言（就本案例而言，宾客是策展人），而不是相反，但这个宿主并不只是接收，而是通过近似翻译和嵌入中文文本与语境来改变宾客语言。漫长的文化相遇史塑造了这种双文化性、东西方的语言共存，或通过日常语言使用完成的共同书写。

en: Liu’s analysis of Goethe’s term

where all nations offer their

himself. And thus every translator should be considered a mediator striving to promote this universal spiritual
and taking it upon himself to make this generalized
go forward. For whatever may be said of the inadequacy of translation, it remains one of the most essential and most worthy activities in the general traffic of the world (italics added by Liu).”
In her discussion of the Chinese translation,

Unlike the latter, who saw himself presiding over a

himself, May Fourth writers turn to European literature largely with the intention of learning how to produce a national canon worthy of being accepted by world literature and being valued by the West.”
As ethnographer-interpreter, I examine the complex intentionalities embodied in the objects that pass through art institutions and the translingual practices that frame them. To speak of
/contemporary art under the weight of proving China’s current place in the world is also to insist on cultural specificity alongside appeals for artistic universality.
zh: 刘禾对歌德1827年创造、后被二十世纪初中国作家采用的“Weltliteratur”（世界文学）一词的分析，以至今仍具洞察力的方式呈现了中国问题。她引用歌德首次使用该词的段落：“懂得并研究德语的人，身处所有民族陈列其商品的市场；他越使自己富有，就越扮演翻译者的角色。因此，每一位译者都应被视为一位中介者，努力促进这种普遍的精神交流，并承担推动这场普遍贸易前行的责任。因为无论人们如何谈论翻译的不足，它仍然是世界普遍交往中最根本、最值得从事的活动之一（斜体为刘禾所加）。”
在讨论中文译词“世界文学”时，刘禾描述了它证明中国在现代国际社会席位的负担：“恰巧，中国作家并不共享歌德对德国语言和文学的乐观信心。歌德看到自己主持一个世界市场，所有民族向他陈列商品，而他慷慨地扮演译者、充实自身；与此不同，五四作家转向欧洲文学，很大程度上是想学习如何生产一种配得上被世界文学接受、被西方珍视的民族经典。”
作为民族志学者兼口译员，我考察穿过艺术机构的物品所承载的复杂意图性，以及框定它们的跨语际实践。在证明中国当前世界地位的重负下谈论“当代艺术”，也意味着在呼吁艺术普遍性的同时坚持文化特殊性。

en: Asia and Our Moment
zh: 亚洲与我们此刻

en: My second stint as interpreter occurred seven months later, when three curators from the Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (ybca) in San Francisco arrived in Beijing. They had shared notes and ideas with Philippe Vergne as part of their preparation and contacted Huang Du, who again served as a local guide. This time I actively prearranged my role in their visit, with everyone’s understanding that it would be part of my fieldwork. When the visiting curators asked me beforehand for input on artists who fell outside the usual circuit, I mentioned the privileging of a largely male avant-garde. At their request, I made arrangements for them to meet with several female artists. In Beijing, René de Guzman, Doryun Chong, and Eungie Joo began a multicity tour of the region that also included Chengdu, Tokyo, Osaka, and Taipei. This trip constituted first-stage research for an exhibition to feature emerging or mid-career Asian artists in China, Japan, Korea, and Taiwan. They later decided to include artists from Thailand as the exhibit took shape under the title

children: Time After Time: Asia and Our Moment

en: (2003). They conceptualized it as an Asian cities show connecting Asia to the location of the museum they represented, the Pacific Rim city of San Francisco with its history of Asian immigration.
zh: 我第二次担任口译是在七个月后，旧金山耶尔巴布埃纳艺术中心（YBCA）的三位策展人来到北京。他们与菲利普·韦尔涅交换了笔记和想法，作为准备工作的一部分，并联系了再次担任当地向导的黄笃。这一次，我主动预先安排了自己在访问中的角色，所有人都理解这将成为我田野工作的一部分。当来访策展人事先问我哪些艺术家处在通常圈子之外时，我提到先锋艺术在很大程度上偏重男性。应他们要求，我安排他们会见几位女性艺术家。在北京，勒内·德古兹曼、Doryun Chong 和 Eungie Joo 开始了一次多城市区域之行，还包括成都、东京、大阪和台北。此行是为一个展出中国、日本、韩国和台湾新兴或中生代亚洲艺术家作品的展览做第一阶段研究。随着展览以《一次又一次：亚洲与我们此刻》（2003）为题成形，他们后来决定加入泰国艺术家。他们把它构想为一个亚洲城市展，将亚洲与他们所代表博物馆所在地——太平洋沿岸的旧金山及其亚洲移民史——联系起来。

en: As Visual Arts Curator of the ybca, René de Guzman had hired Doryun Chong and Eungie Joo as collaborating consultants on the project. He later mentioned that differentiating between their individual interests as curators would “add to the poignancy of what is invariably lost in translation,” noting that his curatorial concerns were largely defined by the goals of the ybca as an institution: “The project for me signifies an attempt at defining an international program that grows out of geo-centric motives.”

With a doctoral degree in Ethnic Studies, Eungie Joo brought to the conversation a commitment to increasing the visibility of U.S. artists of color and challenging institutional rubrics that limit understanding of their work. Doryun Chong’s involvement in the exhibit planning emerged from his training as an art historian of contemporary art in East Asia.
zh: 作为YBCA视觉艺术策展人，勒内·德古兹曼聘请 Doryun Chong 和 Eungie Joo 担任项目合作顾问。他后来说，区分他们各自作为策展人的兴趣，会“加剧翻译中必然失落之物的辛酸”，并指出他的策展关切主要由YBCA作为机构的目标界定：“这个项目对我而言，象征着一次尝试：定义一个从地缘中心动机生长出来的国际项目。”
拥有族裔研究博士学位的 Eungie Joo 为对话带来一种承诺：提高美国有色人种艺术家的可见度，并挑战限制人们理解其作品的机构准则。Doryun Chong 参与展览策划，源自他作为东亚当代艺术史学者的训练。

en: On their first night in Beijing, we met in their hotel bar, where de Guzman gave Huang Du and me some background to the ybca and its goals of serving a city that “has been the primary gateway for infusing Asian peoples into the fabric of America and this region.”

As part of this introduction he mentioned that the San Francisco “South of Market” urban renewal project, where the larger Yerba Buena Center is located, had previously displaced several minority and immigrant communities. I later gained a fuller picture of this project, originally envisioned after World War II as a large-scale commercial convention-sports-office complex that would secure San Francisco’s international importance. Over the years, city business leaders, corporate councils, and elected officials pushed to have the “South of Market” area declared blighted, appropriated from its current residents, and bulldozed to make way for their redevelopment scheme. Decades of neighborhood and union protest, legal wrangling, and political conflict stalled this land-grab until the late 1970s when construction began.
The displaced population included migratory workingmen, dockworkers, warehouse and factory workers, and immigrants—African Americans from the South, Germans, Irish, Greeks, Japanese, and Filipinos.

At the beginning of the twenty-first century, the ybca as a public museum in the center of the redeveloped area was charged with a new mandate to culturally connect the city back to these previously displaced communities.
zh: 他们抵达北京的第一晚，我们在酒店酒吧见面，德古兹曼向黄笃和我介绍YBCA的背景及其目标——服务一座“一直是把亚洲各民族注入美国及本地区肌理的主要门户”的城市。

作为介绍的一部分，他提到旧金山“市场街南”（South of Market）城市更新项目曾迁置若干少数族裔和移民社区，而更大的耶尔巴布埃纳中心就坐落于此。我后来更全面地了解该项目：它最初在二战后被构想为一个大型商业会议—体育—办公综合体，以确保旧金山的国际重要性。多年来，城市商界领袖、企业委员会和民选官员推动把“市场街南”地区宣布为破败区，从其现有居民手中征用，并用推土机夷平，为他们的再开发计划让路。数十年的社区与工会抗议、法律纠纷和政治冲突拖延了这场土地掠夺，直到1970年代末建设才开始。
被迁置人口包括流动工人、码头工人、仓库和工厂工人，以及移民——来自南方的非裔美国人、德国人、爱尔兰人、希腊人、日本人和菲律宾人。
二十一世纪初，作为再开发区域中心公共博物馆的YBCA，负有一项新使命：在文化上重新建立这座城市与这些先前被迁置社区的联系。

en: The ybca curators, like Philippe Vergne, came to China informed by particular institutional motivations that arose, in their case, from San Francisco’s history of striving to become a global city. Its story of dispossession and then attempt at redress presents a picture of complicity between culture and commerce similar to that of “New Beijing.” The curators also informally discussed their personal links to Asia as an additional rationale for their involvement in the exhibition project. René de Guzman and Eungie Joo are second-generation Filipino and Korean Americans, respectively; and Doryun Chong left South Korea in his late teens to pursue higher education in the United States. They narrated abbreviated life histories of immigration and experience as ethnic Americans, as did I, emphasizing a difference in their art world position as Asian American interlocutors.
zh: 像菲利普·韦尔涅一样，YBCA策展人来到中国时，带着特定的机构动机——就他们而言，这些动机源自旧金山努力成为全球城市的历史。它剥夺然后试图补偿的故事，呈现出文化与商业共谋的图景，与“新北京”相似。策展人们还非正式地谈到自己与亚洲的个人联系，作为参与展览项目的额外理由。勒内·德古兹曼和 Eungie Joo 分别是第二代菲律宾裔和韩裔美国人；Doryun Chong 在青少年晚期离开韩国，赴美接受高等教育。他们讲述简略的移民和族裔美国人生活史，我也一样，强调他们作为亚裔美国对话者在艺术界位置上的差异。

en: Are You Among Those Invited?
zh: 你在受邀者之列吗？

en: This intersection of institutional and personal stakes informed the conversations that unfolded during the ybca curators’ visit to Beijing. Persistent themes in these conversations included the struggle for artistic recognition and representation, the role of the nation-state in these struggles, and ambivalence on the part of artists and curators about national identifications. On the one hand, artists may not see themselves and their work as aligned with national ideology. On the other hand, the notions of artist as soldier and artist as dissident are both structured by a modern system of nation-state governance, as are the art institutions that produce artists, curators, and exhibitions.
zh: 机构利益与个人利害的交汇，影响了YBCA策展人访问北京期间的对话。这些对话中反复出现的主题包括争取艺术承认与再现的斗争、民族国家在这些斗争中的角色，以及艺术家和策展人对国族认同的矛盾心理。一方面，艺术家可能不认为自己及作品与民族意识形态一致。另一方面，“艺术家作为战士”和“艺术家作为异见者”的观念，都由现代民族国家治理体系所结构，生产艺术家、策展人和展览的艺术机构也是如此。

en: On their first day of studio tours, Huang Du accommodated multiple demands on his schedule by bringing along another visiting curator. Ute Meta Bauer, a professor at the Institute for Contemporary Art at the Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Vienna, was in town through programming arrangements made by the Beijing branch of the German Goethe Institut. On the previous evening, many Chinese artists I knew had attended the lecture she gave at the institute about her role as cocurator in

. The Documenta exhibitions, presented once every five years in Kassel, Germany, since 1955, serve as surveys of international contemporary art, each distinguished by the programmatic vision of the curator selected to direct the show. Okwui Enwezor, Nigerian by birth, headed

as the first non-Western curator to hold the directorship, and in an unprecedented move, he selected six cocurators to help orchestrate an expanded exhibition concept, consisting of five platforms to take place between March 2001 and September 2002 in locations including Vienna, Berlin, New Delhi, St. Lucia, Lagos, and Kassel.

From what I later heard about Bauer’s talk, many in the audience had pressed her for information about what the curatorial team sought in submissions and whether Chinese work would be represented. The Goethe Institut, whose mission is to promote German language and culture overseas, as the venue for this conversation provides a reminder of the ongoing history of culture and power.
zh: 在他们参观工作室的第一天，黄笃为了兼顾日程上的多项要求，还带上了另一位来访策展人。乌特·梅塔·鲍尔是维也纳美术学院当代艺术研究所教授，因德国歌德学院北京分院安排的项目而来到北京。前一天晚上，我认识的许多中国艺术家参加了她在学院所作的讲座，谈她作为第十一届卡塞尔文献展联合策展人的角色。文献展自1955年以来每五年在德国卡塞尔举办一次，是对国际当代艺术的概览，每届都因被选为总监的策展人的纲领性愿景而独具特色。出生于尼日利亚的奥奎·恩维佐担任第十一届文献展总监，是首位担任该职的非西方策展人；他以前所未有的举动选出六位联合策展人，协助编排一个扩展的展览概念，由五个平台组成，于2001年3月至2002年9月间在维也纳、柏林、新德里、圣卢西亚、拉各斯和卡塞尔等地举行。
从后来听到的关于鲍尔讲座的情况看，许多听众追问策展团队在投稿中寻找什么，以及中国作品是否会被代表。歌德学院的使命是在海外推广德国语言和文化，而它作为这场对话的场所，提醒人们文化与权力的历史仍在继续。

en: Huang Du took us that morning to the apartment studio of Hong Hao, who four and half years earlier had perpetrated an elaborate art hoax as a challenge to the Euro-American centrism of international art and Chinese desire to be recognized by it. In May 1997, he and fellow artist Yan Lei sent out fake
letters, typed in German on letterhead they had meticulously reproduced by silk-screen print, inviting artists across China to participate in a special show called

(Aus der anderen Welt—chinesische Avantgarde). The letter, which was signed Ielnay Oahgnoh (the two artists’ names in pinyin spelled backwards), gave a local contact number to call for more information. When artists rushed to call it, they discovered it connected them to a public telephone booth. The anger of those fooled by the invitations reached such a level that Hong and Yan issued an apology letter in the

art journal. Their prank letter made obvious the host-guest power dynamics at work in the translation of Chinese contemporary art into the “world market” of art. The title of their fake exhibit plays on a Western framing of China as part of a distant, foreign world, not yet coeval with the one into which they send their art. The letter’s signature, a neologistic pun contrived of names spelled backwards, imitates the authorial aura of the foreign word, even if incomprehensible, within a Chinese context. In Hong Hao’s cramped apartment, Bauer handed him a business card. (Huang had briefed her before the meeting about Hong’s history as fake Documenta representative.) Grasping her card in both hands as a gesture of respect, Hong impishly stated that it would now be easier for him to duplicate the logo and start issuing his own Documenta business cards.
zh: 那天上午，黄笃带我们去了洪浩的公寓工作室。四年半前，洪浩策划了一场精心设计的艺术骗局，挑战国际艺术的欧美中心主义，以及中国渴望被其承认的心态。1997年5月，他和艺术家颜磊寄出伪造的第十届文献展邀请函，用他们精心丝网印刷复制的信笺纸以德文打字，邀请全中国艺术家参加一个名为《来自另一个世界——中国先锋艺术》（Aus der anderen Welt—chinesische Avantgarde）的特别展览。信末署名 Ielnay Oahgnoh（两位艺术家名字的拼音倒序拼写），并留下一个本地联系电话供咨询。艺术家们急忙打过去，发现那连接到一个公用电话亭。受骗者的愤怒达到如此程度，以致洪浩和颜磊在《江苏画刊》上发表道歉信。他们的恶作剧信件揭示了把中国当代艺术翻译进艺术“世界市场”时的主客权力动态。假展览的标题戏耍了西方把中国框定为遥远、陌生世界的一部分——尚未与他们送艺术进入的世界同时代。信件署名是以姓名倒拼构成的新造双关，模仿外文词在中国语境中的作者光晕，即便它不可理解。在洪浩局促的公寓里，鲍尔递给他一张名片。（黄笃此前已向鲍尔简要介绍过洪浩假冒文献展代表的经历。）洪浩双手接过名片以示尊重，却顽皮地说，现在他复制标志、开始印发自己的文献展名片会更容易。

en: In the afternoon, the curators headed for the second-floor cafe of Beijing’s Sanlian Bookstore, where the editors of
(Reading), a well-known journal of culture and politics, had organized a roundtable discussion with Ute Meta Bauer and local artists and art scholars.

Daisy Yiyou Wang, a Chinese-born art historian who at the time was pursuing a PhD at Ohio University, served as the Chinese-English interpreter. Bauer began by giving a brief history of Documenta. After World War II, at a time when many German artists had emigrated or been killed, Arnold Bode, a painter and professor from Kassel, hoped to reestablish Germany’s place as a participant in world cultural discourse and international art developments. In 1955, he organized a retrospective of twentieth-century art and presented work that the Nazis had declared degenerate, including artists such as Picasso, Ernst, Arp, Matisse, Kandinsky, and Moore. This vision of cultural exchange on the global level focused, in the first ten exhibits, mainly on Europe and North America. The selection of Enwezor to direct the eleventh exhibition in 2001–2 placed high expectations on his ability to globalize the event.
zh: 下午，策展人们前往北京三联书店二层的咖啡馆，著名文化与政治杂志《读书》的编辑在那里组织了一场与乌特·梅塔·鲍尔及本地艺术家、艺术学者的圆桌讨论。

出生于中国的艺术史学者王伊悠（Daisy Yiyou Wang）当时正在俄亥俄大学攻读博士，担任中英口译。鲍尔首先简要介绍文献展历史。二战后，许多德国艺术家或流亡或遇害，来自卡塞尔的画家、教授阿诺德·博德希望重新确立德国作为世界文化话语和国际艺术发展参与者的地位。1955年，他组织了一场二十世纪艺术回顾展，展出被纳粹宣布为“堕落”的作品，包括毕加索、恩斯特、阿尔普、马蒂斯、康定斯基和摩尔等艺术家。这种全球层面文化交流的愿景，在前十届展览中主要聚焦欧洲和北美。选择恩维佐执导2001至2002年的第十一届展览，使人们高度期待他能让这一活动全球化。

en: The

roundtable conversation gradually turned to the difficulty of organizing shows that claim to be global in reach, since an immediate impulse usually arises to demonstrate adequate representation from all “significant” geographic regions; and artists then begin to suspect curators of basing their selections more on where artists live than on their work. Bauer explained that she had frequently run into this dilemma, for example, at her talk the night before, when she fielded questions about whether or not

would include Latin American or Asian artists. She responded that this identification by geographic lumping doesn’t seem important to most artists, who don’t want to act as national representatives. Philippe Vergne would express a similar sentiment several months later, in March 2002, during a roundtable organized for the opening of the Walker’s
exhibit:
zh: 《读书》圆桌讨论逐渐转向组织号称具有全球覆盖面的展览之困难，因为人们通常立刻想展示所有“重要”地理区域都有充分代表；艺术家随后便开始怀疑策展人的选择更多基于艺术家居住地，而非作品。鲍尔解释说，她经常遇到这一困境，例如前一天晚上的讲座中，有人问她第十一届文献展是否会包括拉丁美洲或亚洲艺术家。她回答说，这种按地理归类的身份认定对大多数艺术家似乎并不重要，他们不想充当国家代表。几个月后，2002年3月，菲利普·韦尔涅在为沃克中心《纬度如何成为形式》展览开幕组织的圆桌讨论中表达了类似感受：

en: What does it mean when you enter a studio in Johannesburg or in São Paulo or in Beijing and say, “I’m here because I’m doing a global show and you’re a global artist”?... Should we conceive of the show as a global show, or should we find a theme around globalization, or should we talk about something else? Is the show about art and practices? I also have the feeling when entering the studios that artists really want to be included in exhibitions about something else. They don’t want to be in a global show.
zh: 当你走进约翰内斯堡、圣保罗或北京的一间工作室，说：“我来这里是因为我在做一个全球展，而你是一位全球艺术家”，这意味着什么？……我们应该把展览设想为一个全球展，还是围绕全球化寻找一个主题，还是谈论点别的？展览是关于艺术与实践的吗？我走进工作室时也有这种感觉：艺术家真正想被纳入的是关于别的东西的展览。他们不想参加一个全球展。

en: Bauer continued by saying she sometimes wished, as a curator, that artists would say no more often if they felt a national or any other ideological framework being imposed on them.
zh: 鲍尔接着说，作为策展人，她有时希望，如果艺术家感到民族或其他意识形态框架被强加于己，他们能更经常地说“不”。

en: Eungie Joo then broke into the discussion to say that for artists marginalized by art world politics, where the odds are already stacked against them, it’s hard to say no. They don’t know when they might get another chance and feel compelled to take whatever they get, even if it’s not ideal.
She also brought up another potential danger for the global ambitions of the Enwezor-directed

by comparing its possible long-term impact to the backlash that occurred after the 1993 Whitney Biennial in New York, labeled by critics as the “politically correct” biennial. Curator Elisabeth Sussman selected artwork that she felt would reach groups not usually drawn to the museum and that reflected debates about multiculturalism, particularly its critiques of mainstream representation and institutional framing. An unprecedented number of artists of color as well as female and gay and lesbian artists exhibited work. Pieces included in the show took on political issues, ranging from the aids crisis to police violence against Rodney King. Attacks against the show, calling it didactic moralizing, lacking in aesthetic and formal value, and even “worthless junk,” came from within and without the art establishment, including a broadside by

Joo characterized this biennial as an antidote used to counteract previous institutional denial on the part of the Whitney, but in a tokenistic way that enabled critics to characterize “minority art” as “bad art.” Once it was all said and done, guilt had been expunged; a commitment to racial or gender justice could be checked off and forgotten; and artists marginalized by the U.S. art mainstream stood in no better position than before. Bauer replied that opportunities to get a foot in the door and gain symbolic capital must be embraced as one way of trying to wedge to door open wider.
zh: Eungie Joo 随后插话：对于被艺术界政治边缘化的艺术家而言，胜算本就对他们不利，说“不”很难。他们不知道下一次机会何时到来，感到只能接受所能得到的一切，即便并不理想。

她还提出恩维佐执导的第十一届文献展全球抱负面临的另一个潜在危险：她将其可能的长期影响，与1993年纽约惠特尼双年展后发生的反弹相比较——批评者当时把该展称为“政治上正确”的双年展。策展人伊丽莎白·萨斯曼选出的作品，是她认为能触及通常不被吸引到博物馆的群体、并反映多元文化主义辩论——尤其是对主流再现和机构框定的批评——的作品。参展的有色人种艺术家以及女性、男同性恋和女同性恋艺术家人数前所未有。展品处理从艾滋病危机到警察对罗德尼·金的暴力等政治议题。对展览的攻击——称其说教、缺乏审美和形式价值，甚至“毫无价值的垃圾”——来自艺术界内外，包括《60分钟》的猛烈抨击。
Joo 把这场双年展描述为一剂解药，用来抵消惠特尼此前的机构性否认，却以一种象征性点缀的方式，使批评者得以把“少数族裔艺术”定性为“坏艺术”。一切尘埃落定后，负罪感被消除；对种族或性别正义的承诺可以打勾然后遗忘；被美国艺术主流边缘化的艺术家处境并不比从前更好。鲍尔回答说，必须抓住踏进门、获得象征资本的机会，作为把门撬得更宽的一种方式。

en: I drew in my notes a schematic of the three discourses that came into conflict in the conversation that afternoon (figure 3.02). While interrelated, these discourses also bear the traces of their historical formation, and tensions remain among them. The Documenta position arises from a German historical moment of skepticism with regard to national politics but a simultaneous desire for Germany to regain a position of world prominence by serving as a Weltliteraturlike platform for cross-cultural exchange between nations. The position articulated by Joo through her example of the 1993 Whitney Biennial presents a kind of diversity nationalism, in which marginalized artists in the United States seek to expand the definition of American cultural citizenship, and thereby make visible the imperialist links between the United States and other parts of the world. The significance of China’s positioning below Europe and the United States hinges on Chinese artists’ ready acknowledgement that no exhibits in China garnered the international attention that Documenta and the Whitney Biennial did. Their desire to emerge on the global stage as a culture capable of commanding the world’s attention represented a conflicted nationalism, of which they were sometimes deeply critical, but that was sustained nonetheless by an art system structured by national institutions.
zh: 我在笔记上画了那天下午对话中相互冲突的三种话语的示意图（图3.02）。这三种话语虽然相互关联，却也带有各自历史形成的痕迹，彼此之间的紧张持续存在。文献展立场源于德国的一个历史时刻：对国家政治持怀疑态度，同时渴望德国通过充当类似世界文学的国与国跨文化交流平台，重新获得世界显要地位。Joo 通过1993年惠特尼双年展所表述的立场，呈现一种多元性民族主义：美国被边缘化的艺术家寻求扩展美国文化公民身份的定义，从而使美国与世界其他地区之间的帝国主义联系变得可见。在图中把中国置于欧洲和美国下方的意义，取决于中国艺术家乐于承认：中国没有哪个展览能获得文献展和惠特尼双年展那样的国际关注。他们渴望作为能够赢得世界注意的文化出现在全球舞台，这代表一种矛盾的民族主义——他们有时深刻批判它，但这种民族主义仍由一个以国家机构为结构的艺术体系所维系。

en: FIG 3.02
zh: 图3.02　相互冲突的国际/国内文化话语。

zh: 图内文字：德国；美国；全球文化交流；多元性政治；中国；争取世界承认。

en: Yan Lei, Hong Hao’s collaborator in the
letter hoax, created that same year a piece titled

children: Are You Among Those Invited to the German Exhibition

en: ? (plate 9). This painting features a Chinese fencer ready to begin a match: one hand poised to pull down a face mask, the other brandishing a sword. An arc of red flags cuts a dramatic diagonal against the blue sky behind her. The symbol repeated on the flag, a lower case “d” with an “x” superimposed over it, is the logo for

. At the top, Yan painted the title question in Chinese characters and pinyin, in a style reminiscent of socialist propaganda posters. He conflates the competition of Chinese artists for invitations to international art exhibits with the desire to compete for one’s country in the Olympic Games. His choice of a female fencer to represent the nation also references the “iron girl” attitude of socialist gender formations, a striking contrast with the overwhelmingly male representation in Chinese contemporary art worlds and a reminder of the gender politics also at play in determining who is among those invited.

Although the ybca curators had requested that I make arrangements for them to meet with several female artists in Beijing, Huang Du disagreed with my recommendations and convinced them not to waste their time on these meetings. After the first one, the ybca curators collectively agreed and asked me to cancel the rest. In his research on professionalization of the arts in post-Mao China, Richard Kraus observes that this process did not as a matter of course lead to liberalization or greater equality. Rather the building of shared structures created exclusionary practices. He cites as example the statistics for Writers Association membership, which show a sharp decline between 1981 and 1988 in the number of women and ethnic minority members, with the male-to-female ratio increasing by a factor of almost seven.
zh: 颜磊——洪浩在文献展邀请函骗局中的合作者——同年创作了《你在被邀请参加德国展览的人当中吗？》（图版9）。这幅画描绘一名准备开始比赛的中国击剑手：一只手准备拉下面罩，另一只手挥舞长剑。一道红旗弧线在蔚蓝天空背景下划出戏剧性对角线。旗帜上重复的符号——一个上面叠加“x”的小写“d”——是第十届文献展的标志。颜磊在画面上方用汉字和拼音写出标题中的问题，风格令人想起社会主义宣传画。他把中国艺术家争取国际艺术展邀请的竞争，与代表国家参加奥运会的渴望混为一谈。他选择女击剑手代表国家，也指涉社会主义性别塑造中的“铁姑娘”姿态，这与中国当代艺术界压倒性的男性代表形成鲜明对比，也提醒人们注意决定谁在受邀者之列的性别政治。

尽管YBCA策展人曾要求我安排他们见几位北京的女性艺术家，黄笃却不赞同我的推荐，并说服他们不要把时间浪费在这些会面上。第一次会面之后，YBCA策展人一致同意，让我取消其余安排。理查德·克劳斯在研究毛泽东之后中国的艺术专业化时观察到，这一过程并未自然带来自由化或更大平等。相反，共同结构的建设制造了排他性实践。他举作家协会会员统计为例：1981至1988年间，女性和少数民族会员人数急剧下降，男女比例几乎增至原来的七倍。

en: Saying No
zh: 说不

en: On November 30, 2001, the ybca curators’ second full day of meeting artists, we drove east of the city center toward the mixed rural-urban Tongzhou District. After three studio visits in the morning, we stopped for lunch at a new two-story restaurant on the side of a dusty road. Around our table sat the three ybca curators, Huang Du, Wang Yin, two other artists from the morning’s agenda, the driver of our car, and myself. I sat stuffing steamed dumplings into my mouth, enjoying a reprieve from my role as interpreter. The beginnings of a lively debate about exactly what I momentarily hoped to escape grumbled in our smoke-filled banquet room. In discussing the unequal parameters of the international art world, in which Chinese artists gained success by inclusion in exhibits in the West but not the other way around, the Chinese artists launched into a complaint about the dominance of English. They described how they often feel misinterpreted or misunderstood when participating in international exhibits but cannot express themselves well enough in English to enter into meaningful conversation.
zh: 2001年11月30日，YBCA策展人用一整天会见艺术家的第二天，我们驱车前往市中心以东城乡交错的通州区。上午走访三个工作室后，我们在一条尘土飞扬的路边一座新开的两层餐馆停下吃午饭。桌边坐着三位YBCA策展人、黄笃、王音、上午日程中的另外两位艺术家、我们的司机和我。我坐着把蒸饺塞进嘴里，享受摆脱口译角色的一刻。一场关于我此刻希望逃离之事的激烈辩论的苗头，在烟雾缭绕的包间里低声酝酿。中国艺术家在讨论国际艺术界不平等的参数——中国艺术家靠参加西方展览取得成功，反过来却不行——时，开始抱怨英语的支配地位。他们描述自己参加国际展览时常常感到被误读或误解，却无法用英语充分表达，以进行有意义的对话。

en: Eungie Joo agreed that a formidable communication gap presents itself at such events and that they as artists have to make certain demands. Drawing on the conversation with Ute Meta Bauer the day before, she said she understood not having the luxury to “say no,” even if the opportunity taken under these conditions might entail inevitable miscommunication, but that they should demand professional interpreters as part of a contractual agreement to participate. She emphasized that contemporary art requires more explanation and contextualization than other forms of art, making adequate translation more imperative than ever. Her foregrounding of a demand to be recognized—to have a voice—is rooted in the U.S. diversity politics strategy of claiming collective injustice in order to lobby for equal representation in the nation and its institutions. But the Chinese artists at the table wanted not just to be included more equally in a U.S. museum but to have the power to produce and interpret contemporary art on their own home ground. For them, more translation does not necessarily change the rules of the game, if the “general traffic of the world” is still directed toward the West.
zh: Eungie Joo 同意这种场合存在巨大的沟通鸿沟，艺术家必须提出某些要求。她借用前一天与乌特·梅塔·鲍尔的对话说，她理解没有“说不”的奢侈，即便在这种情况下抓住的机会可能带来不可避免的误传，但他们应当要求在参展合同中配备专业口译员。她强调，当代艺术需要比其它艺术形式更多的解释和语境化，因此充分的翻译比以往更加迫切。她突出“被承认”的要求——拥有声音——根源在于美国多元性政治的策略：申明群体遭受的不公，以争取在国家及其机构中获得平等代表。但桌边的中国艺术家不仅想更平等地被纳入一家美国博物馆，还想在自己的土地上拥有生产和阐释当代艺术的权力。对他们而言，如果“世界普遍交往”仍以西方为方向，更多翻译未必改变游戏规则。

en: Joo’s use of the phrase “say no” signified having the power to refuse others’ framings, an idea that arose repeatedly in the ybca curators’ conversations. At our lunch table, I translated “say no” in the most literal word-to-word fashion of
rather than the more “native” term
, meaning “to refuse.” Through this choice, I made tongue-in-cheek reference to an anti-U.S. bestseller called

While I did not have time to explain the linguistic genealogy of these two syllables to the curators, the artists at the table recognized it with a knowing laugh. Many Chinese intellectuals critiqued this book as inflammatory nationalist rhetoric, but its mid-1990s popularity represented ambivalence about increased economic and cultural ties between China and the West. The book’s cover depicts the Great Wall guarded by a composite figure with the head of the Statue of Liberty affixed to the body of a military police officer. At the top, the copy reads, “China says no, not to seek confrontation, but for a more equal dialogue.” This book introduced the translated phrase
into everyday Chinese lexicon.
zh: Joo 使用“说不”一语，意味着拥有拒绝他人框定的权力，这一观念在YBCA策展人的交谈中反复出现。在我们的午餐桌上，我用最字面的逐词方式把“say no”译成“说不”，而不是更“地道”的“拒绝”。通过这一选择，我半开玩笑地指涉一本反美畅销书《中国可以说不》。
我虽没有时间向策展人解释这两个音节的语言谱系，桌边的艺术家却会心一笑，认出了它。许多中国知识分子批评这本书是煽动性的民族主义修辞，但它在1990年代中期的流行，代表了对中国与西方经济文化联系日益紧密的矛盾心理。书的封面描绘长城，守卫它的是一个合成形象：自由女神像的头颅接在军警的身体上。上方文案写道：“中国说不，不是为了寻求对抗，而是为了更平等的对话。”这本书把译词“说不”引入日常汉语词汇。

en: It followed a trend of books in Asia about “saying no,” beginning with

children: The Japan That Can Say No

en: in 1989. The high sales of this book in Japan received so much attention in the U.S. Congress, where some used it as justification for trade sanctions against Japan, that it was translated into English.

The phrase “say no” in Japanese is adopted from English, with the “no” untranslated. By turning around American depictions of Japanese social relations as not transparent enough, especially in business negotiations—insinuating that Japanese needed to learn the American practice of “saying no when you mean no”—Sony chairman Akio Morita and politician Shintaro Ishihara critiqued U.S. business practices and advocated greater Japanese independence.

children: The Japan That Can Say No

en: then led to

children: The Asia That Can Say No

en: , coauthored by Ishihara and the prime minister of Malaysia.
The book’s title in English,

children: The Voice of Asia: Two Leaders Discuss the Coming Century

en: , toned down its claim to sovereignty and rejection of the West. The translation of “saying no” into Chinese represents what linguists call a Sino-Japanese-English loanword. Uncertainty about where and how cultural and political nationalism overlap, which caused the laughter at my use of the loan word, troubled the artists’ response to Joo’s insistence on more translators at the table of international art over simply “saying no.”
zh: 它追随了亚洲“说不”书籍的潮流，始于1989年的《日本可以说不》。这本书在日本的畅销在美国国会引起极大关注，有人用它作为对日贸易制裁的理由，于是它被译成英文。
日语中的“say no”借自英语，“no”未加翻译。索尼董事长盛田昭夫和政治家石原慎太郎反过来利用美国对日本社会关系——尤其在商业谈判中——不够透明的描绘（暗示日本人需要学习“想拒绝时就拒绝”的美国做法），批评美国商业实践，主张日本更大的独立性。《日本可以说不》随后催生了石原慎太郎与马来西亚总理合著的《亚洲可以说不》。
该书的英文版标题《亚洲之声：两位领袖纵论即将到来的世纪》淡化了其主权主张和对西方的拒绝。“说不”译入中文，代表语言学家所称的汉日英借词。文化与政治民族主义在何处、如何重叠的不确定性——正是这种不确定性让我使用借词时引来笑声——困扰着艺术家对 Joo 坚持在国际艺术桌上增加口译员、而非仅仅“说不”的回应。

en: Wei Cheng
zh: 围城

en: Wang Yin nodded at my summary in Chinese of Joo’s comments, but then noted with an exhalation of cigarette smoke and raised eyebrows that things were not so easy. Recruiting his teacup as explanatory tool, he laid out his working metaphor for translation as a process that always exceeds the standard tropes of fidelity or natural equivalency that can be discovered between languages, suggesting that more translation may not solve their dilemma. Pointing to his teacup, Wang described any object of translation as a boat, which—he slid the teacup from one spot on the table to another—crosses a river. When tethered to one shore the boat means something different than when docked on the other shore. Even though the materiality of the teacup/boat remains the same, people view it differently, just as Chinese and Western audiences will inevitably “place” his paintings through different conceptual and experiential frameworks.
What the boat means changes because of the journey. He concluded, “It’s like

,” indicating for me to explain this reference to the 1947 novel by Qian Zhongshu popularized by the 1991 television adaptation. In Wang’s invocation of this novel, he reached back to China’s semicolonial past. His besieged city is early-2000s Beijing, with its embassy districts and art galleries catering to expatriate clients, where artists at the table with curators from the United States sought international recognition while remaining wary of inevitable misreadings and accusations of selling out.
zh: 王音听我用中文概括 Joo 的评论后点了点头，但随后吐出一口烟、扬起眉毛说，事情没那么简单。他借茶杯作解释工具，摆出自己关于翻译的工作隐喻：翻译是一个总会超出惯常的忠实隐喻、或语言之间存在可发现的天然对等这一观念的过程，这意味着更多翻译未必解决他们的困境。王音指着茶杯说，任何翻译对象都像一只船——他把茶杯从桌上一个位置滑到另一个位置——渡过一条河。系在此岸时，船的意义不同于停泊在对岸时。尽管茶杯／船的物质性保持不变，人们看待它的方式不同，正如中西方观众不可避免地会通过不同概念和经验框架来“放置”他的画作。
船的意义因旅程而改变。他最后说：“这就像《围城》。”示意我向在场者解释这部钱锺书1947年的小说——1991年电视剧改编使其广为人知。王音援引这部小说，回望中国的半殖民过去。他的围城是2000年代初的北京，有使馆区和迎合外籍客户的画廊；艺术家与来自美国的策展人同桌交谈，寻求国际承认，同时警惕不可避免的误读和“卖身”指控。

en: The artist at his side further explained, “It’s like the saying about marriage at the beginning of
. Unmarried people want to get married. Married people want to get divorced.” In

, Qian Zhongshu uses marriage as a symbol of kinship or fidelity doomed to failure. His female characters embody in turn moribund tradition; whorish, superficial treaty-port culture; and corrupt, materialistic class-based society. The protagonist Fang Hongjian is the bewildered, satirized, individual hero who bounces between them, with the novel’s women in the supporting roles of representing China in all its possible failed incarnations. The gendered logic underlying this extended metaphor is that contemporary (male) artists identify with the protagonist of
zh: 他身旁的艺术家进一步解释：“就像《围城》开头关于婚姻的那句话。没结婚的人想结婚。结了婚的人想离婚。”在《围城》中，钱锺书用婚姻象征注定失败的亲缘或忠诚。他的女性人物依次化身垂死的传统；娼妓式的、肤浅的通商口岸文化；以及腐败、物质至上的阶级社会。主人公方鸿渐是在她们之间弹跳的困惑、被讽刺的个体英雄，而小说中的女性则承担配角角色，代表中国种种可能失败的化身。这一延伸隐喻底层的性别逻辑是：当代（男性）艺术家认同《围城》的主人公。

en: In our banquet room, someone returned to the teacup, stating that if it represented Chinese artwork in international circulation, then Huang Du was the boatman. Huang protested this comparison of him to a middleman, as if it might reduce him to the pidgin of treaty-port compradors like Jimmy Chang in
, who sprinkles his speech with foreign words. When asked, for example, if he collects porcelain, Jimmy responds: “
! Worth quite a lot of money,
. Besides, these things aren’t like calligraphy or paintings. If you can buy calligraphy or paintings which turn out to be fakes, they aren’t worth a cent. They just amount to
. If the porcelain is fake, at least it can hold food” (italics are in English in the original).
For Huang Du, the cultural capital of his cosmopolitan profession resided in the vocabulary of foreign theory:
zh: 在我们的包间里，有人回到茶杯，说如果它代表国际流通中的中国艺术品，那么黄笃就是船夫。黄笃抗议把他比作中间人，仿佛这会把他贬低为《围城》里吉米·张那种通商口岸买办的洋泾浜语——说话时点缀外文词。例如，有人问吉米是否收集瓷器，他回答：“
（当然！去看一看……当然！）值不少钱，
（大把钞票）。再说，这些东西不像书法或画。你要是买了书法或画，结果是假的，一文不值，就是
（废纸）。瓷器是假的，至少还能盛东西。”（斜体部分在中文原作中即为英文；括号内为本译稿所附释义）
对黄笃而言，他世界性职业的文化资本存在于外国理论的词汇中：话语、杂糅、述行性。

en: After so much talk of metaphorical boats and movement of porcelain across the table, Joo asserted that as Asian American curators, she and her colleagues represented a new West, intent on resisting the orientalism she felt their comments suggested. Pointing at her face, she said, “The West looks like this now too.” The Chinese artists did not respond; this suggestion of racial alliance or minority cosmopolitanism did not bridge the gap for them. Doryun Chong, the one curator born and educated in Asia before attending university in the United States, interjected to express hesitancy over the idea of being somehow more authentic culture brokers: “In the United States, I’m called upon as a native expert of Korea or Asia. In Korea, I’m granted certain respect or privilege because of my education in the United States. Can I really exploit both situations and stay honest with myself?”
zh: 谈了这么多关于隐喻之船和瓷器在桌上移动的话之后，Joo 断言，作为亚裔美国策展人，她和同事代表一个新的西方，决心抵抗她感到他们评论中暗示的东方主义。她指着自己的脸说：“西方现在也长这样。”中国艺术家没有回应；这种种族联盟或少数者世界主义的提议，并未为他们弥合鸿沟。Doryun Chong 是唯一在亚洲出生并接受教育、后赴美读大学的策展人，他插话说，对成为某种更本真的文化中介的想法感到迟疑：“在美国，我被当作韩国或亚洲的本土专家；在韩国，我又因为在美受教育而获得某种尊重或特权。我真的能同时利用这两种处境，又对自己保持诚实吗？”

en: Insides and Outsides
zh: 内部与外部

en: All of the arts professionals present at lunch that day were bicultural in their own right. In everyday experience they drew on cultural vocabularies of both Asia and the West and could do so with relative ease. As a group, they arguably had more in common with each other—the global culture of contemporary art and access to its cosmopolitan resources—than with most citizens of their respective nations.

They were all invested in thinking outside the ideological categories of the nation-state. The artists often felt at odds with the Chinese state and its vacillating policies of censorship and sponsorship. The Asian American curators struggled against U.S. institutions of citizenship and national identity framing them as the “unassimilable alien” and worked to create sites of cultural production that remind the nation of its historical ties with Asia in economics, labor, and war.

Yet the different discourses of cultural nationalism that informed their participation in global art led to a subtle polarization over the course of the conversation so that the two sides seemed more in tension than sympathy.
zh: 那天午餐时在场的所有艺术专业人士本身都是双文化的。在日常经验中，他们调用亚洲和西方的文化词汇，并能相对自如地这样做。作为一个群体，他们彼此之间的共同点——当代艺术的全球文化及其世界主义资源的可及性——可以说多于与各自国家大多数公民的共同点。
他们都投身于超越民族国家意识形态范畴的思考。艺术家常感到与中国国家及其摇摆不定的审查与赞助政策相冲突。亚裔美国策展人则与美国公民身份和国族认同制度抗争——这些制度把他们框定为“无法同化的异族”——并努力创造文化生产场所，提醒国家其与亚洲在经济、劳动和战争中的历史联系。
然而，塑造他们参与全球艺术的不同文化民族主义话语，在对话过程中导致了微妙的两极分化，使双方显得更紧张而非同感。

en: The conversation had entered uncertain terrain, where the borders of Asia (as a geopolitical and cultural region) and Asian America (as a geographically based political coalition that deploys notions of a common culture) abraded one other, and where the translation of identity could only be uttered haltingly. For Huang Du, Wang Yin, and the other artists, a sense of fidelity to or kinship with China grew out of a shared language and historical experience of being Third World in relation to the United States or even other parts of Asia such as Japan; theirs was a heroic

(hooligan) nationalism apropos the international stage, where they felt they must prove China worthy of inclusion and by doing so might increase the opportunities currently available to them as culture workers at home. They became comrades in discomfort with their dependency on the West (and its interpreters) for this recognition, even if it is a West with an Asian face. Eungie Joo, Doryun Chong, and René de Guzman, however, might be said to advocate a Pan-Asian fidelity or kinship born of the racialized politics of the United States, where they too felt besieged in relation to a contemporary art world whose exclusivity they challenged. These different versions of who is inside or outside, speaking nearby, represent a moment of coauthorship, but also of fractious claims to oppositionality that strain to recognize one another.
zh: 对话进入了不确定的地带：亚洲（作为地缘政治和文化区域）与亚裔美国（作为基于地理的政治联盟，运用共同文化的观念）的边界相互摩擦，而身份认同的翻译只能结结巴巴地说出。对黄笃、王音和其他艺术家而言，对中国保持忠诚或亲缘感，源于共同语言和作为第三世界相对于美国，甚至日本等亚洲其他地区的共同历史经验；他们的民族主义是面对国际舞台时英雄式的流氓（liumang）民族主义——他们觉得自己必须证明中国配得上被纳入，并借此增加他们作为国内文化工作者目前可获得的机会。他们对依赖西方（及其阐释者）给予这种承认感到同样的不安，并因此成为同志，即便那是一个长着亚洲面孔的西方。然而，也可以说 Eungie Joo、Doryun Chong 和勒内·德古兹曼倡导一种源自美国种族化政治的泛亚忠诚或亲缘感；在美国，他们同样感到被一个他们质疑其排他性的当代艺术世界围困。这些关于谁在内、谁在外的不同说法在彼此近旁言说，代表一个共同书写的时刻，也代表对对立立场的好斗主张——这些主张艰难地试图相互承认。

en: In my blurred role as ethnographer-interpreter, I found myself positioned in different contextual ways: as an imperfect speaker of Chinese who had spent enough time in China to get cultural references like

; as an Asian American intimately aware of racial hierarchies and the fraught politics of inclusion; as a feminist critic of power dynamics in the art world; and as an anthropologist of cultural translations of value. I was aware from the start of disciplinary tensions between art and anthropology. I often tried to reinforce this divide because I did not want to be seen within my research community as an arbiter of aesthetic distinction with the power to provide entrée to Western art spaces. I frequently felt called on by artists to attempt this role, but I resisted it because I lacked institutional art world connections and for fear of seeming partisan to certain individuals. My one attempt to breach this divide, by advocating for more women to be included in the curators’ studio visits, had backfired. The ybca curators’ project description seemed to equate anthropology with orientalism in the following statement: “Wary of the limiting effects of anthropological approaches to contemporary art, we want to disrupt our complicity in the neo-orientalist gaze.” I understood this wariness as emerging from an ethnic studies demand that art be read as art in a universal sense rather than ethnography, for otherwise the Asian in America remains the “unassimilable alien,” a case study in foreign culture rather than cocreator in the kingdom of culture. As an ethnographer of the cultural encounters that produce what is recognized as global contemporary art, and of the aesthetic conventions that shape how those encounters unfold, my goal is not to provide a more historically or culturally accurate way to interpret artworks, but to examine the encounter of conventions as producing art world practices of meaning-making, evaluation, selection, and resistance.

I also remain compelled to account for those art world participants who fell out of the picture. Transnational efforts to speak a shared language of art produce exclusions, the anonymous folk painter in Wang Yin’s studio or the virtually invisible Chinese woman artist.
zh: 在我作为民族志学者兼口译员的模糊角色中，我发现自己以不同方式被语境定位：作为中文不完美、却在中国待得够久、能领会《围城》之类文化指涉的言说者；作为深谙种族等级和包容政治之艰险的亚裔美国人；作为艺术界权力动态的女性主义批评者；作为研究价值之文化翻译的人类学家。我从一开始就意识到艺术与人类学之间的学科张力。我常试图强化这一分界，因为我不想在研究群体中被视为审美区分的仲裁者，有权提供进入西方艺术空间的入场券。艺术家经常要求我尝试这一角色，但我拒绝了，因为我缺乏艺术界机构人脉，也害怕显得偏袒某些个人。我唯一一次试图打破这一分界，是主张让策展人参观更多女性艺术家的工作室，结果适得其反。YBCA策展人的项目说明似乎把人类学等同于东方主义：“由于警惕人类学方法对当代艺术可能产生的限制，我们希望打破自身与新东方主义凝视的共谋。”我理解这种警惕源于族裔研究的要求：艺术应被当作普遍意义上的艺术来阅读，而非民族志；否则，在美国的亚洲人仍将是“无法同化的异族”，是异国文化的案例研究，而非文化王国的共同创造者。作为研究生产所谓全球当代艺术之文化相遇的民族志学者，也作为研究塑造这些相遇如何展开之审美惯例的学者，我的目标不是提供一种在历史上或文化上更准确地阐释艺术品的方式，而是考察惯例的相遇如何生产艺术界意义制造、评价、选择和抵抗的实践。
我也仍感到有责任说明那些从画面中掉落的艺术界参与者。用共同艺术语言言说的跨国努力制造排斥：王音工作室里匿名的民间画师，或几乎隐形的中国女性艺术家。

Huang Du, for example, published a series of dialogues between curators—himself and colleagues from Cuba, Germany, Japan, and the United States—in the Chinese journal

His introduction to the published interviews asserts that curatorial work necessitates nothing less than the globe as its playing field: “In fact, prominent art curators, no matter whether they work from theory to realization, or from realization to theory, must have a macroscopic and global visual field.... Curators play a bridge-like role of enabling dialogue and exchange between artist, the exhibit, and its audience.”

en: I had gone to the center to meet another artist for an interview, but we got waylaid by a group of Belgian university students who had arranged to talk to Wang and several of the artists from his exhibit. The students had funding from their national ministry of culture to investigate contemporary art in China and develop cultural contacts between the two countries but had sparse language skills to do so. I was cajoled into interpreting what was, by now, a fairly familiar conversation. One of the first questions asked by the Belgians was why Chinese contemporary art borrowed so much from the West. The question, in the same breath that it expressed a Western desire for art untainted by the traffic of the world, waiting only to be discovered, also framed Chinese contemporary art as lacking in originality. In the midst of the ensuing discussion, in which several artists took the students to task for their naïve assumption of overwhelming Western influence and Chinese derivativeness, a latecomer, the artist He An, walked in and was brought up to speed. He immediately replied, with a deadpan expression on his face, “I don’t really know anything about Belgium except that you make good guns and now you sell them to the Chinese military.” The students were completely thrown by this display of willful disdain for their country’s culture, which is what they thought they’d come to exchange in the One World Art Center, and the seeming accusation that their nation’s military industry fueled Chinese nationalism. He An’s form of “saying no” underlined the historical legacy that lurks behind Chinese-Western cultural and economic exchange. As the Belgian students scrambled to defend the peaceful ambitions of their small country and the good will behind their visit, He An watched his work of reversals unfold, with a complex intentionality of its own that also had the artists feinting with the shadow of a question that still lingered: Is there a difference between colonization and self-colonization? They had, after all, consented to spend their afternoon hosting a group of curious but uninformed students sent by the Belgian Ministry of Culture.
zh: 我去中心是为采访另一位艺术家，但我们被一群比利时大学生耽搁了——他们安排与王音及其展览的几位艺术家交谈。这些学生获得本国文化部资助，来考察中国当代艺术、发展两国文化联系，却几乎没有相应的语言能力。我被劝说为一场如今已相当熟悉的对话担任口译。比利时人最先问的问题之一是，为什么中国当代艺术从西方借鉴了这么多。这个问题在表达西方渴望未受世界流通污染、只待被发现的艺术的同时，也把中国当代艺术框定为缺乏原创性。在随后的讨论中，几位艺术家责备学生天真地假定西方影响压倒一切、中国只会模仿；这时，迟到的艺术家何岸走进来，被告知了前情。他立刻面无表情地回答：“我对比利时真不太了解，只知道你们枪造得好，现在又卖给中国军队。”学生们被这种对本国文化的故意轻蔑完全打乱了阵脚——他们以为来到一世界艺术中心是为了交流文化——也被那看似指控其国家军工助长中国民族主义的话打乱。何岸的“说不”形式，强调了中西文化与经济交换背后潜伏的历史遗产。当比利时学生匆忙捍卫小国的和平抱负和此行的善意时，何岸看着自己的逆转作品展开，其中自有复杂的意图性，也让艺术家们与一个仍然萦绕的问题之影过招：殖民与自我殖民之间是否存在差异？毕竟，他们同意花一下午接待一群由比利时文化部派来的好奇却无知的学生。

en: In a 1957 speech addressed to China’s youth, Mao Zedong declared, “The world is yours, but it is also ours.” His use of “the world” in relation to who defines it marks a distinction between generations, between the revolutionary founders of the nation and the youthful inheritors of this vision. As a phrase appropriated by contemporary artists, it also registers the difference between world visions, and of what art represents within them, held by various art world participants.

In the next chapter, a monumental art project following the historical route of the Red Army’s Long March demonstrates an ongoing preoccupation with this discrepancy between art worldings. Its curators resurrected Mao Zedong’s revolutionary nationalism to reverse the status quo directionality of art translation efforts. Instead of sending Chinese artists into the Western world, they attempted to draw global attention to Chinese contemporary art by hosting well-known Western artists in China, within the cultural context of world communism. This reconfiguration of global-local relations also nested feminist art encounters within the global-local and East-West encounters that shaped Chinese contemporary art. Again, I found myself drawn in as an interpreter and witness, this time to Chinese female artists finding their own way of “saying no.”
zh: 在1957年对中国青年的讲话中，毛泽东宣布：“世界是你们的，也是我们的。”他对“世界”的用法，以及谁界定世界，标志着代际区分——国家的革命奠基者与这一愿景的青年继承者之间。作为当代艺术家挪用的说法，它也记录了各种艺术界参与者所持世界愿景的差异，以及艺术在这些愿景中所代表之物的差异。

下一章将展示一个沿红军长征历史路线行进的大型艺术项目，它以持续的方式关注艺术世界营造之间的这种差异。其策展人复活毛泽东的革命民族主义，以逆转艺术转译活动既有的流动方向。他们不是把中国艺术家送往西方世界，而是试图通过在世界共产主义的文化语境中邀请知名西方艺术家来中国，把全球注意力吸引到中国当代艺术上。这种对全球—地方关系的重新配置，也把女性主义艺术相遇嵌套在塑造中国当代艺术的全球—地方与东西方相遇之中。再一次，我发现自己作为口译员和见证者被拉入其中，这一次是中国女性艺术家寻找自己的“说不”方式。
